title: Engineering Occupation Categories for CDR
description: Professional Engineer, Engineering Technologist or Engineering Associate: understand the three categories and how to choose the right one.

data.sub: Your category decides the standard your CDR is judged against.

items.title: Professional Engineer
items.text: Typically a four-year engineering degree and broad design responsibility.

items.title: Engineering Technologist
items.text: Typically a three-year degree with applied, specialised work.

items.title: Engineering Associate
items.text: Typically a two-year qualification with practical, supervised work.

sections.heading: How to Choose
paragraphs: Look at your qualification first, then at the level of responsibility in your real work. The category must fit both.
bullets: Length and level of your qualification
Whether you led design or worked under direction
The nominated occupation in your application

sections.heading: Why It Matters
paragraphs: Each category has its own competency standard. A report written for the wrong category can fail to show the right evidence, even when the engineering work itself is strong.
sections.note: Category rules and qualification expectations can change. Confirm them with Engineers Australia before you commit.

items.q: Can I be assessed in a higher category than my degree suggests?
items.a: It is possible only if your qualification and your demonstrated work support it. The assessor judges the evidence, so the claim has to be credible.

items.q: Does my category change the CDR format?
items.a: The parts of the report stay the same, but the competency standard you map to is different for each category.

data.heading: Not sure which category fits?
data.text: Tell us your qualification and role and we will point you in the right direction.
